question: Who disproved the statement, "organic compounds could only be formed within a living system"?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Wohler**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

 
• Friedrich Wohler is best known for the synthesis of urea, an organic compound, from ammonium cyanate, an inorganic salt.
 
• Wohler was a German chemist.
 
• He disproved the statement, "organic compounds could only be formed within a living system"
 
• He was the first to isolate the elements yttrium, beryllium, and titanium.
 
• Wöhler was also known for being a co-discoverer of beryllium, silicon and silicon nitride, as well as the synthesis of calcium carbide.
 
• He was awarded The Copley Medal in 1872.
 
• Copley Medal is awarded by the Royal Society, for "outstanding achievements in research in any branch of science."
 
• Urea, also known as carbamide, is an organic compound with chemical formula CO(NH2)2. This amide has two –NH2 groups joined by a carbonyl (C=O) functional group.
